_comment: Race-safe database next-id (get_next_id) contract -- feature 16. Two owner-
decided fixes (OWNER-DECISIONS.md Batch 4; feature doc 016-database-next-id.md
NEXTID-DEC-01 / NEXTID-DEC-02), each proven against REAL databases with REAL
concurrency (threads / pcntl_fork / Promise.all over independent connections --
NO mocks):
NEXTID-DEC-01 -- the generic next-id TOCTOU + the PostgreSQL first-use race.
The generic sequence fallback did an UPDATE then a SEPARATE SELECT: between
the two, another concurrent caller could increment and commit, so both read
the same post-increment value and returned a DUPLICATE id (a Time-Of-Check-
To-Time-Of-Use race). It is reachable on PostgreSQL because the first-use
bootstrap let two concurrent first-callers each CREATE a separate sequence;
the loser's error was swallowed and it fell to that racy table, drawing an
id from a SECOND, independent counter that duplicated the native sequence's.
Fixed in all four:
* the generic fallback is now a SINGLE atomic statement --
UPDATE tina4_sequences SET current_value = current_value + 1
WHERE seq_name = ? RETURNING current_value -- so the value read is
exactly the one that statement wrote (PostgreSQL supports RETURNING; it
is the engine that reaches this fallback);
* the PostgreSQL bootstrap is CREATE SEQUENCE IF NOT EXISTS + always draw
from nextval(), so two concurrent first-callers share ONE counter and no
caller ever falls to the second mechanism.
NEXTID-DEC-02 -- the MongoDB no-increment. Mongo was broken four ways: PHP's
dedicated path swallowed ANY error into `return 1` (a duplicate-PK collision
with an existing row); Ruby and Node had NO Mongo path at all and fell to the
relational generic path, where the Mongo SET-clause parser matched only
`col = ?` and DROPPED the arithmetic `current_value + 1` (empty $set), so the
counter never advanced and every call returned the SAME id. Fixed in all four:
one DEDICATED atomic path -- findOneAndUpdate({_id: seq}, {$inc:{current_value
:1}}, {upsert, returnDocument:after}) on a tina4_sequences counters
collection, keyed by _id so its built-in unique index makes concurrent
first-use upserts race-safe. PHP no longer returns 1 on error (it raises);
Ruby and Node no longer route Mongo through the relational path.
MAINTAINABILITY (owner directive): one next-id path per backend, ZERO new
runtime dependencies -- the atomic increment reuses each engine's own SQL
(UPDATE ... RETURNING) and the Mongo path reuses the driver already present.
NO MOCKS. Every case drives a REAL database with REAL concurrent callers: the
lab's PostgreSQL :55432 (tina4/tina4), MySQL :3306 (tina4/tina4 -> tina4_test)
and MongoDB :27017. N concurrent callers each on their OWN connection (Python
threads, PHP pcntl_fork children, Ruby threads, Node Promise.all over N
independent adapters); the assertion is N DISTINCT ids. The generic-fallback
case invokes the fallback path directly (its private sequence method) against
real PostgreSQL so the TOCTOU fix is proven where a real client reaches it.
Mutation-proved (all four): revert the generic fallback to the racy
UPDATE-then-separate-SELECT and 'concurrent generic sequence next id yields
distinct ids' goes RED with a duplicate id under concurrency; drop the $inc
(or restore the swallow-to-1 / relational fallback) from the Mongo path and
'mongo next id increments monotonically' goes RED (id2 == id1). Restoring each
returns to green; the atomic UPDATE ... RETURNING and the atomic $inc are
distinct at any concurrency.
Each invariant names a REAL suite file per framework carrying the SAME case
names in each language's own idiom, which scripts/audit-contract-fixtures.py
normalises and matches.
feature: 16 - Race-safe database next-id (fix the generic get_next_id TOCTOU + the PostgreSQL first-use race; give MongoDB one correct atomic findOneAndUpdate($inc) path in all four)

invariants.rule: get_next_id() is ATOMIC: N concurrent callers for the same table, each on its OWN real connection, return N DISTINCT ids -- never a duplicate. This holds on a FRESH PostgreSQL table (the first-use sequence-create race: the loser must share the one native sequence, not draw from a second counter), through the generic tina4_sequences fallback directly (a single atomic UPDATE ... RETURNING, never an UPDATE then a separate SELECT), and on MySQL's per-connection LAST_INSERT_ID sequence path. Identical in all four (Python Database.get_next_id / _sequence_next, PHP Database::getNextId / sequenceNext, Ruby Database#get_next_id / sequence_next, Node Database.getNextId / sequenceNext).
invariants.why: A duplicate primary key allocated under concurrency is silent data corruption -- two rows collide, or an insert fails, at random under load. Proven with a REAL PostgreSQL and a REAL MySQL and N REAL concurrent callers (threads / forked processes / independent async connections), no mocks: the ONLY way N concurrent callers can all get distinct ids is that the increment is atomic. Mutation-proved: revert the generic fallback to UPDATE-then-separate-SELECT and 'concurrent generic sequence next id yields distinct ids' goes RED (a duplicate id under concurrency).
cases: concurrent get next id on a fresh table yields distinct ids
concurrent generic sequence next id yields distinct ids
concurrent get next id on mysql yields distinct ids

invariants.rule: MongoDB get_next_id() ADVANCES and is concurrency-safe: it returns a strictly increasing counter via an atomic findOneAndUpdate($inc) keyed by _id, so id2 > id1 across sequential calls (never the SAME id -- the pre-fix relational fallback dropped the '+ 1', and PHP swallowed errors into `return 1`), and N concurrent callers return N DISTINCT ids. Identical in all four -- one dedicated atomic path reached uniformly (Python routes Database.get_next_id -> MongoDBAdapter.get_next_id; PHP Database::mongoNextId raises instead of returning 1; Ruby MongodbDriver#get_next_id + a Database#get_next_id branch; Node MongodbAdapter.getNextId + a Database.getNextId branch).
invariants.why: A next-id that does not increment hands the SAME id to every caller -- guaranteed duplicate primary keys on Mongo. Proven with a REAL MongoDB, real sequential and real concurrent calls, no mocks: id2 > id1 can only hold if the counter actually advanced, and N concurrent distinct ids can only hold if the $inc is atomic. Mutation-proved: drop the $inc (or restore the swallow-to-1 / relational fallback) and 'mongo next id increments monotonically' goes RED (id2 == id1).
cases: concurrent mongo next id yields distinct ids
